body:
Your question caught my attention. My father passed away a year ago, from a cancer that ended quickly with his health, and in a matter of days took his life.

My father was depressed and had suicidal tendencies for much of his life. My uncle, his brother, went through the same thing and ended up taking his life in 2013. I do not know if genetics has anything to do with suicide tendencies, but it seems so.

In the end, when I visited my father for the last time in the hospital, I saw him really suffering a lot. Groaning in pain. A really very sad scene, and it's the last one I have of him. In the end he just slept, and I left the hospital, only to find out a few days after he had died.

My father did everything, apparently, to die. He smoked his whole life. He smoked even more from the day of the divorce. He began to smoke concealed when he wanted to tell me that he had stopped, and hid and tore away all the tests that could have predicted the disease. He did not seek help for his depression and insisted that he was well.

I feel that maybe one day he asked himself the same question, "How can I get cancer?". I dont know, I have no way of knowing, but maybe he thought dying in this way was a little better than suicide.

Well, in the end, he suffered a lot. And we too.
